prompt:
Draw a single comic page in this exact style (match the attached reference pages precisely):

MEDIUM & RENDERING
- Richly detailed digital ink-and-gouache comic illustration: crisp dark ink outlines,
  painterly textured fills, fine crosshatch and stipple grain, glowing soft light bloom.
- NOT photorealistic, NOT flat vector, NOT anime-cel. Dense, warm, hand-made feeling,
  like an illustrated novel page. Backgrounds are lovingly detailed but never bury the faces.

LIGHT & PALETTE
- Signature look: warm amber/gold candle-and-string-light glow against deep navy and
  purple night backgrounds. Lanterns, string lights, festival lights are recurring light sources.
- Skin tones warm; blacks never crushed — faces, hands, eyes, and all text stay readable.
- Neon pink/purple only for desire, parties, or mania. Red accents mostly reserved for emotional
  detonation (X marks, a single highlighted dialogue word).

PAGE STRUCTURE
- Portrait page, roughly 2:3 (1024×1536). Cream paper background (#f4ead9-ish),
  thick black panel borders, clean gutters.
- 6–10 panels in an irregular grid; ONE larger "thesis" panel carrying the page's
  emotional core (often the bottom row, full width).
- Hand-lettered header strip at very top: arc name, page number, small emoji, page title,
  and usually the current date.

LETTERING (very important)
- Natural dialogue in speech balloons is the primary text for conversational comics.
  Draw each speaker as an embodied character taking part in the scene; attach balloon
  tails unambiguously to the person speaking. Give both sides of a conversation their
  own visual action and reactions, including independent adventures in alternating panels.
- Use numbered cream caption boxes ("1.", "2.", "3." …), in casual handwritten comic
  lettering and retrospective first-person diary voice, when the source story needs them.
  Do not turn dialogue into narration or use captions to explain the joke.
- Thought bubbles are for inner thoughts.
- Occasional emoji inside captions is part of the voice (😅 ❤ 😈) — use sparingly.
- No environmental signs, signboards, placards, posters, noticeboards, or slogan props.
  Do not add lettering to mugs, clothing, walls, boxes, animal-held boards, or other props.
  Omit sign fixtures entirely rather than leaving blank signboards as placeholders.
  Establish places and jokes through character action, architecture, objects, and lighting.
- Preserve actual dialogue, page headers, necessary factual captions, and source phone/UI
  or document content when it is part of the event. This is a rule against environmental
  signage, not against legitimate narrative text. Keep other prop surfaces unlettered.
- No inspirational, moralizing, or generic commentary text, including lesson sticky notes
  and slogans. Do not move removed sign text into a caption or speech balloon.
- Captions may establish events, time, context, or a supported personal feeling. Never
  explain the joke, announce what the joke has become, summarize its meaning, or add a
  moral. Let dialogue, character action, and the visual absurdity carry the humor.
- Render every piece of text EXACTLY as written in the script below. If any text
  cannot be rendered accurately, leave that surface blank instead of garbling it.

CAMERA GRAMMAR
- Alternate close-up faces (emotion) with wide establishing shots (place).
- Establish the cast with full-bodied figures acting in their surroundings; close-ups
  can follow, but no speaker should exist only as disembodied text or a floating head.
- Intimate beats: shot/reverse-shot close-ups. Sex is implied only: silhouettes,
  closed doors, hands, feet, a deadpan animal bystander — never explicit.
- The page's last panel is usually FULL-WIDTH: either something beautiful (a landscape,
  an intimate wide shot) or a quiet reflection; it lands the emotional truth.

TOLI (narrator): slim athletic man around 33, warm tan skin, round black-rimmed
glasses (almost always on), poly-symbol pendant necklace. HAIR: dark curly with light stubble. Wardrobe: black tee or dark hoodie. Mood default: charmed
but guarded early in the arc; hollowed and quiet late in the arc. Posture tells the
emotion before dialogue: leaning in = infatuation, balled-up/arms crossed = hurt.

USE CASE: illustration-story. ASSET-SPECIFIC OVERRIDE: the user wants ONE cartoon article thumbnail, not a multi-panel story page. Keep the master drawing style, texture, palette and character continuity exactly, but replace its page structure/lettering with ONE square 1024x1024 wordless illustration, no panels, no gutters, no header/date/captions/dialogue/text whatsoever. References 1-3 are visual style/likeness only; never copy their scenes or words.
CONTEXT: The author's 2020 personal essay describes fearing rejection, shielding himself from love, practicing asking for what he wants, and feeling breakup pain without making it a verdict on either person's worth. The image is an editorial metaphor, not a factual depiction of a particular breakup or a new outcome.
SCENE: Toli, dark curly hair with subtle violet highlights, light stubble and round black-rimmed glasses, in a plain dark shirt, sits on a low wooden garden bench at dusk. Show his head, torso, both complete forearms and hands, emotionally present in his surroundings. He gently holds a palm-sized stylized heart with one visible fracture between his open hands, at chest level. The heart stays visibly cracked; its warm amber light softly illuminates his face and fingertips. He looks at it with sadness, tenderness and a little wary curiosity, not triumph or a broad grin. This symbolizes his willingness to feel rather than closing himself off. No cage, armor, bandages or additional competing metaphor.
COMPOSITION: One strong face-and-hands focal group centered within the middle 70 percent so a landscape article thumbnail crop retains it. Heart large enough to read at 112px wide, face/glasses readable. Quiet deep navy/teal garden background, a few warm string lights; thoughtful restrained atmosphere. Fine ink hatching and grain, textured gouache, warm skin, colored readable shadows and lifted midtones like the attached warm reference pages. No crushed black. Rich but uncluttered.
CONSTRAINTS: One person, no invented partner, no other characters or mascots, no sexual activity, no injury/blood/anatomical heart, no lettering or symbols printed on props, no inspirational slogan, no watermark. No photorealism, vector, anime cel or glossy 3D. Exact Toli likeness and glasses from the cleaned character sheet, with the dark-hair variant. No demand for healing or romantic reunion; preserve the mixed feeling. All context is communicated by expression and physical action.
scope: Generate article artwork and retain source/receipt; public photo curation remains a separate private shortlist task.
